note: Description taken from Sands' 1965 revision (in English), including the alate and soldier; the worker is not treated separately; the original description is Sjöstedt 1896 (Ekundu, Cameroon). The synonymy is complex; Sands newly synonymizes 5 species names and notes that most earlier records of 'Eutermes arborum' belong to this species. The OCR misread decimal points as hyphens or colons (e.g. I-39 for 1.39, 0:79 for 0.79), restored here by magnitude; illegible means are not cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A rather large species (alate head width 1.43—1.70, soldier head width 0.73—1.35); the differences from N. arborum are given under that species; Sands places all five names pius, incurvus, ueleensis, indoensis and expulsus in the synonymy of this species (syn. n.).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule deep chestnut-brown to dark brown, slightly paler in front of the ocelli, postclypeus yellowish brown, labrum yellow, antennae brown; pronotum dark brown with a slightly paler spot in the middle of the anterior half, meso- and metanota and the remaining thoracic sclerites dark brown; legs yellow, the ends of the femora and the bases of the tibiae brown; abdominal tergites dark brown, the sternites dark brown at the sides and paler, yellowish brown, in the middle; wing membrane semi-transparent brown, the veins dark brown, with 1 dark brown line on the inner side of the radius sector. Posterior margin of the head capsule behind the eyes regularly rounded but less than a semicircle; frontal marks inconspicuous and variable: from Y-shaped and slightly paler than the head capsule to almost absent or even slightly darker than the head capsule; compound eyes almost circular, moderately to distinctly prominent relative to their own diameter but not large relative to head width, eye width index 2.9—3.4; ocelli medium-sized, from 2/3 of their own least diameter to distinctly further from the compound eyes; postclypeus weakly inflated, 3.3—4.2 times as wide as long, anterior margin slightly concave or weakly wavy, posterior margin convex, bluntly angled at the middle, nearly straight or slightly arcuate towards the outer corners; antennae 15-segmented, II and IV about equal and slightly longer than III and V (the latter two also about equal). Female cerci slightly papillate-conical, shorter than the basal width. Measurements (25 specimens, 7 localities, mm): head width (across the eyes) 1.43—1.70 (mean 1.54); greatest diameter of the compound eye 0.44—0.55 (mean 0.49); ocellus 0.11—0.15 × 0.13—0.21 (mean 0.13 × 0.18); ocellus to eye 0.08—0.13 (mean 0.10); pronotum width 1.18—1.43 (mean 1.32); pronotum length 0.70—0.88 (mean 0.79); hind tibia length 1.75—2.13 (mean 1.93); fore wing length 11.40—13.10.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule orange-yellow to ferruginous orange, nasus ferruginous orange to chestnut-brown; pronotum and antennae concolorous with the head capsule; abdominal tergites and femora yellow, sternites, tibiae and tarsi pale yellow. Head capsule in frontal view varying with body size: oval and narrowing anteriorly in small individuals, almost circular in medium ones, in the largest broader than long to the base of the nasus, the midline of the back of the head often depressed, sometimes with small tubercles at the sides of the base of the nasus; nasus weakly to moderately conical. In lateral view distinctly concave, the back of the head elevated and smoothly rounded (except in the smallest individuals), often wavy with a weak elevation at the base of the nasus; nasus from distinctly shorter than to distinctly longer than the rest of the head capsule measured from the posterior margin of the antennal bases (even within one colony), nasus cone angle 5—17 degrees; postmental plate slightly convex; antennae 12—14-segmented, usually 13-segmented, the proportions varying with body size, III long, up to twice II, IV and V about equal and slightly longer than II. Cephalic bristles confined to the hairy tip of the nasus and to bristles all over the postmental plate, the dorsum of the head capsule without prominent bristles. Measurements (144 specimens, 35 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.40—2.11 (mean 1.93); head width 0.73—1.35 (mean 1.07); head capsule depth 0.53—0.95 (mean 0.76); pronotum width 0.38—0.65 (mean 0.50); pronotum length 0.13—0.38 (mean 0.21); hind tibia length 0.93—1.73 (mean 1.26).
